result.scope_note: The claim involves two time spans: (1) from the signing of the Constitution in 1787 to the ratification of the Bill of Rights in 1791 (~4 years), and (2) from the congressional proposal of the Bill of Rights in 1789 to its ratification in 1791 (~2 years). Both dates are well-documented, allowing direct comparison.

explanation.text: The Constitution was signed on September 17, 1787, in Philadelphia, establishing the start date for the first period.
Congress proposed the Bill of Rights on September 25, 1789, marking the beginning of the second period.
The Bill of Rights was ratified on December 15, 1791, which ends both time periods under comparison.
The duration from the Constitution's signing in 1787 to the Bill of Rights' ratification in 1791 is approximately 4 years and 3 months.
The duration from the congressional proposal of the Bill of Rights in 1789 to its ratification in 1791 is approximately 2 years and 3 months.
The first duration exceeds the second, supporting the claim that the years from the 1787 signing to 1791 ratification were longer than from proposal to ratification.
